O.outcome_detail: engagement and being hooked by participatory group self-expression

cells.quote: We think that jazz bands persist as a school and after-school activity because they offer students something quite different from playing in a school orchestra — opportunities to master complex technical skills such the art of improvisation in a participatory, group context. Jazz is the sound of freedom; it is an opportunity to explore personal expression in social context.
cells.note: The authors present this as an interpretive argument based partly on their own experience as students and parents, not as a controlled comparison.

D.treatment: participation in a school jazz band

O.outcome_detail: continued participation for five or more years

cells.quote: In our own experience of school jazz bands, both as students and as parents of children, the reason students get hooked on jazz band and continue with it for 5 or more years has almost nothing to do with academic goals nor parental pressure.
cells.note: This is a narrative claim from the commentary authors' experience; the text reports no empirical effect estimate or formal comparison.

O.outcome_detail: output quality on tasks inside the model’s capability frontier

cells.quote: Field-experimental evidence sharpens the same point. In a preregistered experiment with 758 professional consultants, access to GPT-4 raised output quality by roughly 40 per cent on tasks inside the model’s frontier of capability, yet made consultants 19 percentage points less likely to produce correct solutions on a task engineered to sit just outside it (a ‘jagged frontier’ that the participants proved systematically poor at perceiving (Dell’Acqua et al. 2026)).
cells.note: The study text identifies a preregistered experiment but does not state random assignment, session duration, or the consultants’ target-domain expertise.
